enhanced.fullText:
The Davis-Bacon Act, codified at 40 U.S.C. §§ 3141-3144, 3146, and 3147, mandates prevailing wage requirements for federally funded construction projects exceeding $2,000. This legislation, originally enacted in 1931 and significantly amended by the Davis-Bacon Act Reform Act of 1988, applies directly to higher education institutions receiving federal construction assistance through programs such as Title III HBCU Capital Financing, NSF research facility grants, and other federal infrastructure funding.

Under 40 U.S.C. § 3142(a), all laborers and mechanics employed by contractors and subcontractors on covered construction projects must receive wages no less than the prevailing rates established by the Department of Labor for the locality. The Department of Labor publishes these wage determinations under 29 CFR Part 1, incorporating them into all applicable contracts. Higher education institutions must ensure compliance when using federal funds for dormitory construction, laboratory renovations, campus infrastructure improvements, and similar projects.

The Act's scope encompasses "construction, alteration, or repair" as defined in 29 CFR § 1.3, including painting, decorating, and mechanical/electrical work. Universities must include specific Davis-Bacon clauses in all applicable construction contracts, as required by 29 CFR § 5.5(a). These clauses mandate contractor compliance with wage determinations, weekly payroll submissions, and employee classification requirements.

Enforcement mechanisms include contract termination, debarment proceedings under 29 CFR Part 5, and withholding of contract payments. The Department of Labor may impose back wage liabilities and exclude non-compliant contractors from future federal work for up to three years under 40 U.S.C. § 3144. Universities face potential loss of federal funding for systematic non-compliance.

Recent regulatory updates include the 2022 amendments to 29 CFR Part 1, enhancing wage determination accuracy and expanding apprenticeship program recognition. The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021 increased Davis-Bacon coverage for broadband and other technology infrastructure projects common in higher education settings. Institutions must monitor ongoing regulatory developments through the Federal Register and Department of Labor guidance.
enhanced.summary: Davis-Bacon Act requires universities to ensure contractors on federally funded construction projects over $2,000 pay prevailing wages per DOL determinations, include mandatory contract clauses, and maintain compliance documentation.
enhanced.requirements:
## Contract Administration
- Include Davis-Bacon clauses per 29 CFR § 5.5(a) in all applicable construction contracts
- Obtain current wage determinations from DOL before contract execution
- Verify contractor understanding of prevailing wage obligations

## Wage Compliance Monitoring
- Review weekly certified payroll reports from contractors per 29 CFR § 5.5(a)(3)(ii)
- Conduct periodic on-site interviews with workers to verify wage payments
- Document all wage compliance activities in project files

## Project Coverage Determination
- Assess federal funding sources exceeding $2,000 threshold per 40 U.S.C. § 3142
- Evaluate construction scope under 29 CFR § 1.3 definitions
- Consult DOL guidance for mixed-funding project applicability

## Enforcement Response
- Report suspected violations to DOL within 30 days of discovery
- Withhold contract payments pending wage dispute resolution
- Coordinate with federal funding agencies on compliance issues
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No direct reporting to federal agencies required from institutions. However, universities must maintain certified payrolls from contractors, document compliance monitoring activities, and report suspected violations to Department of Labor promptly upon discovery.
